versions.changelog:
software-engineering-discipline 2.0.1

- Expanded scope: Skill now applies explicitly to implementing features, bugfixes, refactoring, code review, and test/coverage evaluation.
- Strengthened RED LINES: Must verify all APIs/configs before use (guesses flagged as escalation, not acceptance); stricter on test signals—no skipping, quarantining, blindly updating snapshots, or hiding failures.
- Refined trade-off guidance: Explicitly allows user-directed abstraction/refactoring even when simpler options exist, but restricts unprompted over-structuring; clarified real vs. mechanical scope in commits.
- Added explicit test strategy requirements: Map risk to appropriate test boundaries, favor direct evidence, and clarify when E2E/integration/unit/contract tests should be used.
- Improved delivery/handoff standards: Explicit flagging of `[UNVERIFIED]`, confirmation that executed checks prove the claim, and more rigorous proof for behavior, error modes, and blast radius.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.
Agent-runtime rewrite. See repo for details.

Agent-runtime rewrite: RED LINES (hazard-gated, never-skip) + verify-before-use rule (fixes hallucinated API/config) + red-line/preference split + correct trade-off bias (agents over-abstract) + binding delivery gate with attached test output. Dropped SE-theory exposition models already know. Net shorter (103->84 lines).

Agent-runtime rewrite: added RED LINES (hazard-gated never-skip limits), verify-before-use rule (fixes hallucinated API/config), red-line vs preference split, correct trade-off bias, and a binding delivery gate with attached test output. Dropped SE-theory exposition. Net shorter.

v1.1: trimmed lecture into observable constraints; fixed SDP-vs-DIP, OCP/if, rule-of-three, validation-vs-assertion; added §7 Large-System Hazards (concurrency/idempotency, data migrations, backward-compat, failure design, perf budget, security edges); added concrete skip conditions; commit hygiene + naming + observability detail.
Initial release: 7-section engineering discipline for coding agents on large complex codebases.
